**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 36, verse 31:**

﴿Have they not seen﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, who say to the Prophet ﴿you are not a messenger﴾. The interrogative (*istifham*) here is for *taqrir* (an affirmative question that asserts what is already known), meaning: they know. ﴿How many﴾ (*kam*) is *khabariyya* (informative, meaning "many"), and what follows it governs it, but it is *mu'allaqa* (suspended, prevented from governing what precedes it). The meaning is: We destroyed before them ﴿many generations﴾ (*qurun*), that is, nations, ﴿that they﴾, i.e., those destroyed, ﴿to them﴾, i.e., the deniers, ﴿do not return﴾. Will they not take warning from them? And *anna* (that) is a *badal* (substitute or apposition) for what precedes it, in accordance with the meaning mentioned.

"And not" (wa-in) is a negative particle, or it is the lightened form (in-na, "indeed"), (wa-in) ... "all" (kullun) means all creatures, and it is the subject (mubtada'). "Lamma" with the doubled mim is in the sense of "only" (illa), or with the single mim (the lam is then a distinguishing lam (lam al-faraqa) and ma is extra (mazidah)). "All" (jami') is the predicate of the subject, meaning they are all gathered (majmu'un). "Before Us" (ladayna) means with Us, at the place of standing after their resurrection. "Brought forth" (muhdarun) for the reckoning is the second predicate.

And in one qira'a it is read with the ta' (تَعْقِلُونَ), addressing them directly.

﴿And We did not teach him poetry﴾, i.e., the Prophet. This is a refutation of their claim that what he brought of the Qur'an is poetry. ﴿Nor is it befitting for him﴾, i.e., poetry does not come easily to him. ﴿It is not﴾, i.e., what he brought is not, ﴿but a reminder﴾, i.e., an admonition, ﴿and a clear Qur'an﴾, i.e., one that makes clear the rulings and other things.

[Tafsir al-Jalalayn on 36:70]

﴿That he may warn﴾ with the yā' and the tā' (i.e., "liyundhira" read with yā' or "litundhira" with tā', both readings), ﴿whoever is alive﴾ (yaʿqil, i.e., one who understands what he is addressed with), and they are the believers. ﴿And the word will be justified﴾ (with the punishment) ﴿against the disbelievers﴾, and they are like the dead, who do not understand what they are addressed with.

(Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 36, verse 71:

﴿Do they not see﴾ meaning, do they not know? The interrogative (al-istifham) is for confirmation (al-taqrir), and the waw (and) that precedes it is for conjunction (al-'atf).

﴿that We created for them, of what Our hands have made,﴾ We made it without partner or helper.

﴿cattle﴾ they are camels, cows and sheep.

﴿so they are masters of them﴾ controlling them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 36, verse 72:

﴿And We made them subservient to them⟩ we subjected them to them ﴿so some of them they ride⟩ their mount (markub)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 36, verse 73:

﴿And for them therein are benefits﴾ such as their wool, their hair and their fur, ﴿and drinks﴾ from their milk; it is the plural of mashrab, meaning either the act of drinking or its place. ﴿Will they not then be grateful?﴾ to the One who bestowed these upon them, so that they would believe; i.e., they have not done that.

And they took besides Allah ﴿gods﴾, idols which they worship, ﴿so that they might be helped﴾, that is, be protected from the punishment of Allah the Exalted, through the intercession of their gods, as they supposed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 36, verse 75:

﴿They are not able to help them﴾, i.e., their gods are treated as if they were rational beings, ﴿while they are a host (ready) for them﴾, i.e., their gods, the idols, ﴿brought forth﴾ into the Fire along with them, ﴿while they are a host for them﴾ according to their own claim that they would help them.

So let not their speech grieve you (ﷺ): that you are not sent, and other than that. Indeed We know what they conceal and what they reveal, of that and other than it, and We will recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 36, verse 77:

﴿Have they not seen that We created him from a drop of semen?﴾ [He means] he knows, and he is al-'As ibn Wa'il. ﴿Then behold, he is an open adversary.﴾ [He is] one who is extremely contentious toward Us, ﴿clear [in his argument]﴾, having expressed it in denying the resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 36, verse 78:

﴿And he presents to Us a parable﴾ concerning that, ﴿and forgets his creation﴾ from the semen, which is more wondrous than the parable itself. ﴿He says, "Who will give life to the bones when they are decayed?"﴾ i.e., crumbled to dust. It does not say "rameemah" with a ta' marbutah because it is a noun (ism), not an adjective (sifah). It is narrated that he took a decayed bone and crumbled it, and said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Does Allah give life to this after it has rotted and disintegrated?" So the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yes, and He will cause you to enter the Fire."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 36, verse 79:

﴿Say: He who brought them into being the first time will give them life again, and He is Knowing of every creation.﴾ [He is] the Knower of every created thing, both in summary and in detail, before its creation and after its creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 36, verse 80:

﴿The One who made for you﴾ among mankind ﴿from the green tree﴾ the marakh and the 'affar, or every tree except the 'unnab (jujube), ﴿fire, so that from it you kindle﴾ you strike (sparks). This is an indication of His power over resurrection, for He has gathered in it water, fire and wood: the water does not extinguish the fire, nor does the fire burn the wood.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 36, verse 81:

﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth,﴾ despite their greatness, ﴿able to create the like of them?﴾ That is, the human beings in smallness. ﴿Yes indeed!﴾ That is, He is able to do that. He answered himself. ﴿And He is the Creator,﴾ the One who creates much, ﴿the Knowing﴾ of everything.

﴿Indeed, His command﴾ means His affair, ﴿when He intends a thing﴾ meaning, to create a thing, ﴿is that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ meaning, so it comes into being. In another recitation (qira'a), the verb فَيَكُونَ (fayakūna, "and it is") is in the accusative (naṣb, the grammatical case that marks the verb here), coordinated (ʿaṭf) with يَقُولَ (yaqūla, "He says").

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 36, verse 83:

﴿So glory be to He in whose hand is the dominion (malakut) of all things, and to Him you will be returned﴾ — malakut: "mulk" (dominion), with the waw and the taa' added for emphasis (lil-mubalaghah), meaning the power over ﴿all things﴾; ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾: you will be sent back (turaddun) in the Hereafter.
